items.note: The signed exchange (X_a,Y_a)->(-Y_a,X_a) with restored scratch, and the net change (JV+RG)x, follow the paper's proof. But S1.1 calls all three stages forward invocations, while the paper's stage 2 is the inverse schedule from Y to X (S1.1.3 gets this right). The central coefficients (|S∩T| mod 2, (|S∩T|-1)/2) that the side wires cancel are never given.

The plan only alludes to lifting the network 'through frames' and to 'the frame identity' with frame Phi_M. It never states D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1}, the per-route operator, or the fact that a common frame commutes with a pointwise gate.

The comparable labels, the only decreasing edges (center 3->4, loss h), the telescoping to Wm-2N+2L and the ratios 100/539 and 101/539 are all stated correctly. The gate-label table and the residual computation behind them are only named in the method, not shown. L=Ich is implicit, and the orthonormal-basis part of the lemma is not covered.

The projection assignment, the -P_{U_a} sources, rank(P_V-P_U)=dim V-dim U and the endpoint difference I_m all match the paper. The plan gives only s_b<W_b m, not s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b. It also omits the N source edges with matrix 2P_{U_a} (rank one, zero dimension change), which is why the rank sum has -N rather than -2N.

The route matches the paper: weight additivity mod 4, one kernel aI+bX_v per orthonormal residual vector, zero/full labels giving I and C^{⊗m}, and a Z repair of X_a->Y_a. The exact rank sum s_c=W_c m-2N+2L_c is replaced by s_c<W_c m, and the k-column extension is not stated.
S1.5 states s_b/W_b<m^tau and s_c/W_c<m^sigma with tau=sigma=1-2^{-50}, and S1.2.4 gives L/N<1/2. The deficits eta_b, eta_c and the log m<20 estimate are only pointed to by the quote, not shown.
Linear-time triangular updates, cyclic row splitting and offset cyclic shifts are used in passing, and elementary-stream-ops and controlled-shift are listed as dependencies. Neither lemma is stated.

Both lemmas are stated correctly and derived along the paper's route. The factorization uses the topmost-row, rightmost-entry pivot. The shear is built from triangular transforms in O(V) plus one interchange per one of Pi (two controlled shifts and one interchange). Choosing the prime q is only implicit.

The sub-steps follow the paper's proof: cyclic row split, Phi_M frames giving Phi_{I_m}, the three-shear interchange, s calls on V/W, F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), and the depth-first parking schedule. The statement says 'given enough rows' instead of 'a row field of length divisible by W^k' (S2.4.1 mentions W^k).

The high digits form a row field padded to a multiple of W^k, the remaining width is cut into base-m pieces given to the power-width procedure, and [2^u] is padded to [q^e]. This is the paper's proof. The unequal-width remark (1737-1762) is not covered.

The edge formula P_M(prod C_{e_j}^{eps_j})P_M^{-1}, the s_c children on e/m axes and H_0^{⊗D}=b^D S_D C^{⊗D} S_D are correct. Missing: the inverse-child identity (C^{-1})^{⊗f}=(-i)^f Z^{⊗f}C^{⊗f}Z^{⊗f}, which keeps every child a forward call, and the conjugation P_M X_v P_M^{-1}=X_{Mv}.

The eight parity-conditioned additions, the cyclic shifts, the bad set of fraction delta_bad, the sort-based repair and the separate top bit all follow the paper. The cost O(V(L^tau+1)) is given without the full bound or the parameter-family conditions. The chunk swaps that move the target chunk, which are the source of the L^tau term, are absent from the method.

The node overhead O(V((eK)^tau+1)), the rows from the first q_0 chunks with u=Wg+w, and F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1) are stated correctly. The unrolling is asserted, not shown: leaves at e<d^beta, K<=e^{c/beta}, the base-m pieces and the condition max{lambda, sigma+beta(1-sigma)}<lambda' are all missing.

The layer H_0^{⊗D} on one selected bit per chunk, its O(V d^{lambda'}) cost, exact dyadic evaluation and the single truncation with error <√2·2^{-p} all match the paper. The guard width ⌈C_0 d^{C_1}⌉=o(p) is only asserted: the depth recurrence A(e)<=sA(e/m)+E and the constants are not shown.

The bit-reversed stored order (B_tF_t^-, F_t^+B_t^{-1}), the prefix-slot moves O(TpdK), the at most Dq-1 chunk exchanges and the total cost are correct. Missing: the character cancellation F^+F^-=t^{-1}I, the exact counterpart LBF^-_t and the error bound √2·ℓ·2^{-p}. The plan also says every round is a simultaneous layer, but prefix-slot rounds are processed individually.

This is the paper's signed Kronecker substitution: evaluation at B_0=2^{4p}, four products with the established multiplier, centered residues with |h_j|<B_0/2, negacyclic reduction, and a shift by p+ℓ, at cost O(rp log(rp)).

The steps are the paper's: keep the common LB order, take signed-packed pointwise products, apply the opposite procedure, scale by M, check F^-(f*g)=M(F^-f)(F^-g), and get error <√2·M(3ℓ+1)·2^{-p}. The cost matches.

The exact identity P_sF_s=2^{2α^2}B_0P_tF_tA is derived as in the paper: the Gaussian identity, the Neumann-series inverse of N, A=S', B_0=D'J'C. Tensoring and axis exposure are covered too. The algorithms for Ã and B̃_0, with error <p^2 and time O(t p^{3/2+δ} α), are stated but not derived.

Cancellation of R (F^+R_c=R_c^{-1}F^+, commuting with pointwise products, two normalizations giving (u*v)/S^2) is derived faithfully. The Bluestein identity QF_t u=ā·(a*(ā·u))/T, with chirp a=exp(-πi Σ s_i j_i^2/t_i), is never stated. S6.4 only uses its computed form.

b, p=6b, d, K, t_i∈{r/2,r}, the sizes, the prime intervals, T/2<S<T and the absence of wraparound are correct. The values eta=1/(4d), alpha=⌈(12d^2b)^{1/4}⌉ and gamma are not given. The existence of the primes (Rosser–Schoenfeld via HvdH Lemma 5.1) and the check alpha^4 theta_i>p are asserted, not shown.

The map x->prod x_i^{mu_i}, its isomorphism, the triangular mixed-radix update in order i=d..1 as prefix-controlled cyclic shifts, the axis reordering by chunk swaps and the cost O(Tp d^2(1+ℓ^tau)) all follow the paper. The explicit formula b_i is only described in words.
x_d->ζy with ζ=e^{πi/r}, well defined since (ζy)^r=1, the wrap-sign cancellation, M_C=(f*g)/T, and exact phase products truncated once all match the paper.

The source transform (A, chirp transform, B_0, scale 2^gamma, exact counterpart RF_s) and the step sequence of the algorithm match the paper. The input scaling of digits by 2^{-b-2}, which the factor 2^{2b+4} undoes, is not mentioned. Nor is defining the opposite-sign procedure by complex conjugation.

The error-propagation framework, the pointwise-product error (2E_s+2)h_p, E_w, rounding below 1/2 and the carry recurrence are correct. The decisive numbers are missing: E_s=9·2^gamma·TL, E_w<28·2^gamma·T^2L and the final bound 448b·2^{-b+gamma}<=448b·2^{-3b/4}<1/2, which rests on gamma<=b/4 and p=6b.

The normalized cost rows, the setup bounds, the absorption of log p powers into p^kappa and the final O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}) all match. The table of seven powers and their margins g_i is not listed. min g_i=2^{-181}=2kappa is asserted without identifying g_2=eps·c·(1-tau) as the binding one.
S0 claims to disprove the n log n optimality conjecture in the model. The plan does not explain what an eventual lower bound would assert, or why liminf T(n)/(n lg n)=0 refutes it.

errors.says: Three forward invocations of the subset-intersection network, at stages 1, 2 and 3, send (X_a,Y_a) to (-Y_a,X_a).
errors.paper: Stage 1 and stage 3 are forward invocations from X to Y; stage 2 is the inverse forward schedule from Y to X, effecting X<-X-Y (the plan's own S1.1.3 and motivation say 'subtract').

errors.says: Method: take projections onto the labels as the frames, so an edge difference P_V-P_U has rank equal to the dimension change.
errors.paper: The frames are the address permutations Phi_M with M=P_U. The first edge on each X_a has matrix 2P_{U_a} of rank one where the dimension change is zero, giving the -N (not -2N) in s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b.

errors.says: Method: every edge is a shear that costs rank-many half-width interchanges.
errors.paper: Each chunk of e=m^k digits is split into m fields of b=e/m digits; the recursive interchanges have width e/m, not half the width.

errors.says: Each of the ℓ rounds is one simultaneous butterfly layer on all participating axes.
errors.paper: The leading round h=ℓ-1 acts only on the long axes, and rounds on prefix slots are processed individually by bit moves and paired scans. Only the rounds in the K-bit chunks use the simultaneous layer.

chain: The tree follows the paper's route to the main bound in order: scalar exchange network, labels, the two interfaces with s<Wm, power-width and arbitrary-width interchange, the simultaneous layer, synthetic transforms and convolution, resampling with permutation cancellation, CRT and twist, assembly, exact recovery and cost accounting. It thins out where the paper's quantitative core lies. The common-frame identity is only alluded to. The exact rank sums s_b and s_c, the guard-width and recurrence unrolling for the layer, the Bluestein chirp identity, the Gaussian approximation algorithms, and the explicit error constants and margin list are asserted rather than derived.
